author: BrentDesk Staff
headline: Mobedex sells interiors into Jeddah's residential market from a website advertising last year
deck: The interiors show running alongside JIBEX addresses a real market through a channel that has not been updated since 2025.
excerpt: Mobedex runs concurrently with JIBEX in Jeddah covering furniture, doors, flooring and smart home technology, though its own website still advertises 2025 dates.
content:
Mobedex runs alongside JIBEX at the Jeddah Centre for Exhibitions and Events from 15 to 17 September, covering furniture, paints, doors and windows, hotel equipment, flooring, smart home technology, curtains and home textiles. Its own standalone website still advertises April 2025 dates, more than a year out of date, so every detail available about the current edition comes from the JIBEX site instead.

That is unfortunate, because the market it addresses is substantial. Jeddah's residential stock is large and ageing, and the interiors categories Mobedex covers — furniture, doors, flooring, textiles, paints — are bought both for new construction and for refurbishment, with the second market considerably less cyclical than the first.

The refurbishment side deserves more attention than it usually receives in Saudi construction coverage. This publication's reporting concentrates, reasonably, on new build: giga-projects, residential programmes, industrial capacity. But a housing stock of Saudi Arabia's size generates continuous demand for replacement kitchens, bathrooms, flooring and joinery, and that demand is served by small contractors buying from distributors rather than by main contractors buying on specification. It is a different channel with different products and different margins.

Smart home technology on the exhibitor profile is the category with the most movement. Home automation has moved from a luxury specification to a mid-market expectation across the Gulf, driven by falling hardware costs and by residential developers using it as a differentiator. It also creates an installation and support requirement that the traditional interiors trade is not set up to provide.

Hotel equipment appearing in Mobedex's categories is an overlap worth noting, since the Riyadh hospitality cluster running on exactly the same dates covers the same ground at considerably greater depth, with a published exhibitor list, a named speaker programme and dedicated shows for interiors and lighting. A Jeddah buyer with a hospitality requirement has a straightforward choice between them, and it is not obvious that the co-located Jeddah offer competes.

Both shows run evening hours, 16:00 to 22:00, which suits a trade audience attending after their own working day and reflects a buyer profile of owners and small contractors rather than corporate specifiers.

The organiser is Icon International with KAC. Sponsors named for the combined event include Saudi Red Bricks, Petromin Foton, Reef and, for the China pavilion, CBGG and Zhejiang.

Category and sponsor detail is taken from the JIBEX site; no exhibitor list, visitor figure or floor area has been published for either show. For a supplier the refurbishment channel is steadier than new build and considerably less visible in published market data.
